content_voiceover: This slide lays out the modern classification of Hodgkin lymphoma and the immunophenotype that separates its two major forms. Under WHO-HAEM5, Hodgkin lymphoma splits into nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma and classical Hodgkin lymphoma, and classical Hodgkin lymphoma has four subtypes you should be able to rattle off: nodular sclerosis, lymphocyte-rich, mixed cellularity, and lymphocyte-depleted. Now here's the twist the slide is flagging: the 2022 International Consensus Classification, the ICC, renamed nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma to nodular lymphocyte predominant B-cell lymphoma, essentially demoting it out of the Hodgkin family because biologically it behaves like a B-cell lymphoma. The immunophenotype proves the point. The neoplastic cell in that entity is the LP cell, the popcorn cell, and it's CD3 negative, CD20 positive, CD45 positive, CD79a positive, CD15 negative, CD30 negative, PAX-5 positive, and BCL6 positive, essentially a normal B-cell marker profile. Contrast that with the Reed-Sternberg cell of classical Hodgkin lymphoma, which is CD3 negative, CD20 negative, CD45 negative, CD79a negative, but flips to CD15 positive, CD30 positive, with only weak PAX-5. That CD15 and CD30 positive, CD45 and CD20 negative pattern is the single most tested immunophenotype in Hodgkin lymphoma.
keypoints: WHO-HAEM5: NLPHL vs classical HL (nodular sclerosis, lymphocyte-rich, mixed cellularity, lymphocyte-depleted)
ICC 2022 renamed NLPHL to nodular lymphocyte predominant B-cell lymphoma
RS cell (classical HL): CD15+/CD30+, CD20-/CD45-/CD79a-, PAX-5 weak
High-yield: CD15+/CD30+ but CD45- and CD20- = classical HL signature
keypoint_voiceover: Lock in two immunophenotypes. The LP or popcorn cell of nodular lymphocyte predominant disease is CD20 positive, CD79a positive, CD15 negative, CD30 negative, essentially a B-cell profile, which is why the ICC 2022 stripped the Hodgkin label and renamed it nodular lymphocyte predominant B-cell lymphoma. The Reed-Sternberg cell of classical Hodgkin lymphoma flips that: CD15 positive, CD30 positive, but CD45 negative, CD20 negative, and only weak PAX-5. That contrast is exam gold.
